newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool prices maintain their rise.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool prices maintain their rise.

text.p: Australian wool prices maintained their recent rate of sales in Sydney and Fremantle this week, the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said on Friday.
The Wool International (WI) eastern market indicator rose 19 cents to 678 cents per kg clean over the week.

The Australian Wool Exchange (AWEX) northern and western indices ended the week at 967 and 951 respectively, increases of 26 and 46 points. The southern index was unchanged at 924 with no sale in the southern region this week. A total of 56,923 bales were offered with a pass in rate of 8.9 percent. The comprised 6.7 percent in Sydney and 10.8 percent in Fremantle.

Market fundamentals were essentially unchanged with relatively limited supplies of wool facing widespread competition from all trade sectors, led by European and Japanese buyers, it said. The current strength of demand saw WI sell a further 20,000 bales of stockpile wool, including further quantities for delivery in the September and December quarters.

This was a positive sign of increasing trade confidence in the market, AWEX said. Overseas reports continue to confirm that the wool textile pipeline is re-filling following the rundown in inventory levels which occurred in response to subdued retail demand in recent seasons, it said.
However, the key to sustaining prices and pipeline demand will be the level of retail sales in the coming northern hemisphere autumn/winter season, AWEX said.

Growers who have held wool back from sale so far pending an improvement in prices have started to respond to recent price trends with the offering for next week's auction sales up by more than 30 percent or 18,000 bales on the figure originally rostered by AWEX, it said.
Sales continue next week in Sydney and Melbourne with 72,200 bales rostered for sale.
